recipe.name: Lomo Saltado
recipe.description: A Peruvian beef stir-fry of seared, soy-marinated sirloin with red onion, jalapeño and just-warmed tomatoes in a tangy soy and vinegar sauce.

ingredients.ingredient_name: Sirloin tips, trimmed and sliced into 3-inch (7.5 cm) strips
Ground black pepper, for the marinade
Grapeseed or neutral oil, for the first batch of beef
Grapeseed or neutral oil, for the second batch of beef
Grapeseed or neutral oil, for the onion
Red onion, cut into 1/2-inch (1 cm) half rings
Jalapeño chili, thinly sliced into rounds

steps: Toss the sirloin strips in a medium bowl with the cumin, salt, pepper and the soy sauce for the marinade. Let them sit on the counter for 10 minutes.
Pat the beef dry with paper towels.
Heat the oil for the first batch in a large skillet, 12 inches (30 cm) across, on high. Sear half the beef in one layer until browned, 2–3 minutes per side.
Lift the beef out to a plate. Sear the rest in the oil for the second batch, 2–3 minutes per side until browned, then remove.
Add the oil for the onion to the same skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the red onion, stirring, for 2 minutes until softened.
Pour in the red wine vinegar and the soy sauce for the sauce. Scrape the base of the skillet and simmer for 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Stir in the garlic and jalapeño for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the beef and its resting juices to the skillet and add the tomatoes. Stir for 30 seconds until the beef is heated through.
Taste, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve at once.
You nailed it! Grab a plate and dig in.
